Variants.Content: The unique legend of the Lys family of Moja rarely survives, and the real weight of the family name comes from the shared life of Pentos' urban elite: caravan shares, mansions, debts, kinship marriages and the patronage of public feasts. It cannot rely on large fiefdoms to monopolize its subjects like the lords of Westeros, and can only continue to manage wealth and peer support. Pentos maintains superficial order by the prince and governor class, but its real power is often hidden in merchant houses, debts, marriages and mercenary contracts. The treaty with Braavos prohibited open slavery and limited armaments, but the wealthy still circumvented the rules with indentured servants and complicated names.
Entry Moharis The high position here is not the natural right that comes with a fiefdom, but the fragile balance maintained by wealth and peer recognition.

Entry Moharis If a rich family pays their bills on time and does not hoard food when the harvest is poor, others will praise them; if a rich family only shows its generosity with lavish banquets, the poor will soon see through it.

Entry Moharis Moha Lys is a powerful family of Pentos, and its status relies on trade, debt, marriage alliances and long-term operations within the governor class. The family crest is just a facade, the real weight of the family is whether they can protect their fiefdom, honor their engagements, and rally people in times of crisis.
